name: Hati

facts.text: Hati is a level-69 named with 30,000 health at the door of Iarnvidiur's chamber, beside Skoll.
He bites (Hati's Bite) and mesmerizes everyone in a 450 radius for 29 seconds.
Allakhazam lists Hati as humanoid, level 65; he drops a moonstone-studded axe.
In Norse myth Hati chases the moon and Skoll the sun until Ragnarok.

story:
In the old songs Hati is the wolf who runs after the moon, as Skoll runs after the sun, and one day he will catch it, and the nights will be dark for good. Snorri calls him the son of Hrodvitnir, which is another name for Fenrir. Whether the Hati of the lair is that wolf or a pup of Iarnvidiur's brood who was given the name and grew into it, nobody in Midgard can say, and the dwarves say it does not matter: a name is a thing you live up to.

He has lived up to it. He walks on two legs now, more often than not, and he carries his mother's patience. Where Skoll runs at things, Hati waits for them to fall asleep. His howl is the long silver one, and anyone who hears it close stands dreaming for half a minute, eyes open and unseeing, while he bites. Raiders who have been under it say the dream is always the same: a cold white light low on the horizon, and something running after it.

He and Skoll lie at their mother's door like hounds at a hall, and nothing passes them to reach her. They have never caught the moon, and they do not seem to mind. The iarn dwarves say that is because they are not in a hurry. The old one's brood never is. They are waiting for the end of the world, and the end of the world has always been coming.

When Hati dies, his howl breaks off in the middle. The dwarves say that on those nights the moon over Aegir looks a little larger, as if it had slowed down to look back.
legend: Hati's mez covers a big circle and lasts half a minute, so keep cure-mez ready and don't stack the casters. Kill him and Skoll before you open Iarnvidiur's door, or they join her. They're close together, so pull them as a pair and split the tanks: one on Hati, one on Skoll. Hati's bite hits hard on whoever is asleep, so wake the mezzed fast. The skalds say if Hati ever catches the moon, the nights will be dark for good. His moonstone axe is a nice drop. Fight both wolves at the door, never inside the old one's room.

loremasterTopic.text: The moon-chaser of the old songs, or a wolf of [Iarnvidiur]'s brood who took the name. His long silver howl puts whoever hears it close to sleep.

bookPage: From Thorgrim of Faraheim's notes. An iarn dwarf hunter told me she once fell asleep under Hati's howl and lived, because her husband carried her out. She said the dream was a white light low on the edge of the world, and that she was running after it on four legs, and that she was happier than she had ever been. When she woke she wept, because she was a dwarf again. She said she understands now why the wolves are not in a hurry. She said the running is the point. She said she goes to the edge of the wood some nights to listen.
